text.p: The following stories were reported in Lithuanian newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The economy ministry decided to cut electricity supply to 10 municipalities until they provide a list of companies which have not paid their bills.
- Newly-appointed prosecutor general Kazys Pednychia, 46, said he will focus on financial fraud cases.
- Lithuanian officials reassured EU Commissioneer Hans van den Broek that all the neccessary security measures will be taken in Ignalina nuclear power plant.
- A forum of foreign investors criticised the country's tax and customs systems.
- Troubled State Commercial bank reported 172.7 million litas of losses in 1996.
- Parliament decided to allow the privatisation of Lithuanian Telecom, oil extracting company Geonafta, Lithuanian Sea Shipping, Kedainiai Chemistry plant and Panevezys Glass.
- The Centre Union started to initiate an amendment to the Constitution to citizens who do not reside permanently in the country to be a candidate to the presidential office.
- The president of the International Olympic Committee Juan Antonio Samaranch arrives in Vilnius on Saturday on the invite of President Algirdas Brazauskas.
- Biggest insurance company Lietuvos Draudimas said its net profit in 1996 more than doubled to 19 million litas.
- Lithuania failed to collect 271 million litas in the 1996 budget.

- Preliminary data showed the finance ministry has collected 447.8 million litas in revenues in March, 38.7 million litas more than planned but was 82.2 million litas below the target for the first quarter of 1997.
